subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Auction Fever
description: Learn Auction Fever in one minute.

hook.text: A painting estimated at $5,000 sells for $22,000 at auction. The winner regrets it the next morning.

buildup.text: Auction fever is the emotional escalation that occurs during competitive bidding.

discovery.text: The winner's curse: the winning bidder likely overestimates the item's value.

twist.text: eBay's countdown timer amplifies fever. Sniping in the last seconds triggers panic bidding from those who thought they.

climax.text: Set a maximum bid before the auction starts. Write it down. When the fever hits, stick to the number.

punchline.text: If winning feels thrilling, you probably overpaid.

quiz.question: What is the winner's curse in auctions?
options: The winner gets the item at an unfairly low price
The winner likely overestimated the item's value by beating all others
The auction house takes an excessive commission

details.summary: Auction fever describes the emotional escalation that occurs during competitive bidding, where the excitement of winning and fear of losing drive bidders to pay far more than their pre-auction valuations would predict.
details.whyItMatters: Auction fever explains why winning bids routinely exceed the item's market value. Understanding this phenomenon helps bidders set firm limits and helps auction designers create environments that maximize revenue.
takeaways: Competitive arousal drives bidders beyond their planned maximum price
The desire to win can override rational valuation during bidding
Setting strict pre-auction limits is the best defense against overbidding

faq.question: What causes auction fever psychologically?
faq.answer: Competition triggers arousal and loss aversion simultaneously. Each rival bid frames not-winning as a loss, and the social pressure of public bidding amplifies the emotional need to prevail over competitors.

faq.question: Is auction fever different from the winner's curse?
faq.answer: Related but distinct. Auction fever is the emotional overbidding during the process. The winner's curse is the realization afterward that you overpaid. Auction fever is a cause; the winner's curse is its frequent consequence.
